_doc: CLEANROOM-1 (Rowan, 2026-11-25): 'everything has to work together automatically and seamlessly from the beginning ... it has to all bootstrap autonomously.' Read by foundation/cleanroom.py. A sandbox tenant is built from nothing but seed/ and the idea below, booted, run for a simulated day and torn down. Every capability below must come up with zero human steps; a capability that does not is a finding filed as Q-CLEANROOM-<id>, closed only by `python3 -m foundation cleanroom --probe <id>`.

# Idea

A living, encyclopedic replication ledger across many fields that tracks which published findings were re-tested, keeps every entry current as new replications appear, and reports what went stale each week.

# System test

- Loop: new replication found, entry updated, stale entries re-checked, with no person in the middle
- Measure: entries older than their review window, target 0
- Upkeep: new studies and replications are published every week
- Run cost: 5 USD a month for the back end

# Who it is for

- Researchers and readers who need to know what held up

# First outcomes

- Every new replication is linked within one day
- No entry is more than a month past its review date
- A weekly report lists what changed

# Constraints

- Budget per month: 5 USD

capabilities.what: the bootstrap runs every stage without a blocked one
a hosted boot opens no card that asks a person for a secret, token or key
the repository resets its own settings (delete branch on merge) and cleans branches
every workflow declares budget, trigger, free alternative and a timeout, and honours HALT
credentials come through the platform's own path (host or consent screen), never pasted
D1, Worker and cron are declared and the provision plan is written
the tick Worker and its loops exist
a public page is served at /
portfolio, product and project managers and a reviewer are staffed
objectives and the liveness metrics are seeded
the system keeps a knowledge graph of its own data
the system serves its manifest and joins the directory
the system questions what it does not know (inverted lenses, pre-mortem, red team)
the system files its own improvement and research work
every declared fault has an exercised drill
the fresh seed meets its own definition (doctrine/system.json): every part names code that exists, SYSTEM.md is current and imported
what the seed publishes for people passes the human-voice lint
a simulated day of ticks runs with no error
after a simulated day the system has computed its own ignition stage from evidence and is at least ticking; what blocks the next stage is named
the sandbox is torn down and leaves nothing behind

_criticality_doc: A sandbox has no deploys, money or models, so it cannot reach critical: k_eff needs verified deploys. The sandbox proves the stage machinery runs and names its blocker; critical and self-sustaining are read from live systems (/health ignition stage, python3 -m foundation seedadmit --autonomy).
